items.claim: A reflected or stored cross-site scripting entry point is confirmed when a chosen script payload executes in the page context rather than being escaped into inert text.
items.body:
In practice on HTB this shows up as: Web Application Penetration Testing is a vital part of any penetration test. It plays an essential role in identifying critical vulnerabilities that may lead to the organization's assets being compromised. Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities are among the most common vulnerabilities in any web application, with studies indicating that over 80% of all web applications are vulnerable to it. An XSS vulnerability may allow an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript code within the target's browser, leading to various types of attacks, including compromising web admins and their web applications.

Write-up provenance: Esther7171/HackTheBox-Writeups-Walkthroughs :: Write-ups/Academy/05. Web Exploitation/27. Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)/Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).md (713 words, classified web).
items.disproof: Refuted when the payload is returned HTML-encoded with no executable sink, which shows the output is contextually escaped rather than vulnerable.
